A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same AdaVD research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices can be compared reliably despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-erasure experiments, CS/FID comparisons, runtime measurements, and appendix evaluations of nudity erasure, transferability, hyperparameters, and failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SDv3 demonstrations, SAFREE comparisons, and expanded quantitative results.

M1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds an SDv3 adaptation: CLIP embeddings still use the final subject token, while T5 embeddings use the mean of real-word tokens, broadcast across positions. The core orthogonal value decomposition and adaptive shift remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover instance, art-style, celebrity, and I2P nudity erasure, alongside the same multi-concept and downstream tasks. The added SDv3 illustrations remain within existing cartoon-instance coverage; they introduce a model configuration rather than a distinct dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds SAFREE to the art-style comparisons in Table 5 and Appendix F.1. The existing ConAbl, MACE, SPM, NP, SLD, and SuppressEOT comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation with the SDv3 transformer backbone and extends metric coverage to target-concept FID and non-target CS. Existing template counts, ten images per template, SDv1.4 sampling settings, and the NudeNet threshold remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns of the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 and Figure 13 extend the transferability analysis to a transformer denoiser with T5 embeddings. Earlier token-masking, hyperparameter sensitivity, 1–40-concept scaling, and Starry Night failure-case analyses are retained, although relocated and visually rearranged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify matching random seed 0 across methods, in v1 Appendix G.1 and v2 Appendix C.1. Neither adds repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands reported results with full CS/FID matrices, SAFREE scores, and SDv3 images, while main Tables 1–3 remain identical. Some repeated values differ without explanation: ConAbl's Anne Hathaway FID after Bruce Lee erasure changes from 48.08 in v1 Table 4 to 40.95 in v2 Table 6. Its Dog FID for three-instance erasure remains 31.59 in Table 1 but appears as 23.83 in new Table 4. These are reporting differences, not established performance improvements.

T1.justification: The method equations, linear-independence assumption, and projection derivations are retained. v1 Appendices E.1–E.2 become v2 Appendices B.1–B.2. The newly numbered cross-attention equation was already stated inline in v1.

C1.justification: The main claims remain training-free, precise, low-cost erasure through orthogonal value decomposition and adaptive shifts, including the claimed 2–10-fold prior-preservation advantage and applicability across models and downstream tasks. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about interpreting target FID and non-target CS in Appendix D.1, although it incorrectly associates lower FID with greater visual change. Appendix F.1 adds an overgeneralized second-best erasure claim: Table 5 shows SAFREE has lower target CS than AdaVD for Picasso and Monet. Earlier failure mechanisms and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 supplies concrete encoder-specific preprocessing instructions for reproducing the SDv3 adaptation, including averaging T5 real-word embeddings. Existing SDv1.4 defaults, hardware information, and code-access information are retained; moving implementation details from G.1 to C.1 is otherwise organizational.

R1.justification: v2 introduces SAFREE as concurrent work and distinguishes its text-embedding operations and hard removal control from AdaVD's value-space operations and soft shifts. It also adds the T5 reference. Other reference updates largely concern publication metadata.

P1.justification: The appendix is substantially reorganized: derivations move from E to B, implementation and sensitivity analysis from G to C, and experiments are regrouped into D–H. The appendix roadmap is removed, several opening passages are rewritten, and affiliations, correspondence information, and acknowledgements are updated.

P2.justification: The appendices change from two-column to single-column presentation. Expanded tables introduce paired CS/FID columns and gray secondary metrics; sensitivity and multi-concept figures are rearranged; and SDv3 Figure 13 is added. Earlier qualitative images are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The SDv3 adaptation and demonstrations strengthen evidence of portability, while the relevant SAFREE comparison and fuller tables make the empirical conclusions easier to assess. These gains are limited by inconsistent repeated values, the mistaken FID interpretation, and the overstated SAFREE ranking. Overall, the additional validation provides a modest improvement, with the original headline results and statistical support essentially unchanged.
